item.title: She went to college to become a social worker. Now she's joined the skilled trades
item.description: While the rise of AI continues to fuel the debate over whether college is worth the cost, apprenticeships in the skilled trades are having a moment, drawing in people of all backgrounds including college graduates.

item.title: Nearly two million people are behind bars in the US. How did we get here?
item.description:
Lynn Novick's new, four-part PBS documentary series, Crime and Punishment in America, goes inside the U.S. prison system and explores how
our approach to criminals has changed over time.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy to face a new trial in spring of 2027 over children's killing
item.description: A new trial is set in Massachusetts against Lindsay Clancy as prosecutors seek a criminal conviction over the killing of her three young children.

item.title: Air traffic controllers' union head on the nationwide ground stop
item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep asks the head of the air traffic controllers' union what it was like for controllers as the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop.

item.title: These birds fly 17,000 miles every year. Climate change could make it harder
item.description: Migratory birds cross the entire globe, carefully timing their journeys with the seasons. In a hotter climate, that timing is increasingly out of sync.

item.title: They saw people losing food benefits. So they started handing out free groceries
item.description: The cuts and changes to SNAP have been difficult for government workers who take pride in helping others. In San Diego, workers said they couldn't sit back while their neighbors went hungry.

item.title: Affordability was a key issue for midterm voters. It helped make childcare one, too
item.description: Childcare costs have surged, putting a major financial burden on U.S. families. Advocates say the subject once on the fringes of political debate became a major issue during the midterms.

item.title: Far from home. Voyager 1 is now farther than anything man has sent into space
item.description: NASA's Voyager 1, which is the furthest man-made object from Earth, is set to reach a new milestone this week. On Wednesday, the probe will be roughly 16 billion miles from Earth.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: New Orleans port sues owners of tanker involved in Mississippi crash
item.description: Officials are seeking at least $1 million in damages from the owners of the tanker that hit a cruise ship last week. The incident was dubbed "the miracle on the Mississippi" after no one was killed.
